status_note: A bug in the documentation. The engine's behaviour (PL-3) was closed as intended on 2026-11-05 ([#30594](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/30594)), so the `truediv` Notes and the user guide's IEEE 754 claim are what is wrong. Unchanged on main (35a2cb73, 2026-11-04). No docs issue found.
title: Docs: float division by a literal or one-row divisor does not follow IEEE 754 as documented
summary: The documentation says float division follows IEEE 754, and division by a literal or one-row divisor does not. Pages: `Expr.truediv` (https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/expressions/api/polars.Expr.truediv.html, py-polars/src/polars/expr/expr.py#L6928-L6933 at py-2.1.0), Notes: "Zero-division behaviour follows IEEE-754", with 0/0 NaN and n/0 ±infinity; and the user guide (https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/concepts/data-types-and-structures/#floating-point-numbers, docs/source/user-guide/concepts/data-types-and-structures.md#L176-L190): Polars "generally follows the IEEE 754 floating point standard", with NaN ordering and the sign of zero or NaN as the listed exceptions.

With a length-1 divisor, `/`, `//` and `%` multiply by the reciprocal (crates/polars-compute/src/arithmetic/float.rs#L78-L119, PL-3). A nonzero finite divisor then creates NaN and infinity: `0.0 / 1e-310` is NaN (IEEE 0.0), `1e-300 / 1e-310` is inf (IEEE 1e10), and `49.0 % 49.0` is 49.0, outside `[0, |y|)`. The user guide's accuracy paragraph ("does not provide guarantees on the error") covers the ulp in `49.0 / 49.0 = 0.9999999999999999`; it does not cover a NaN from two finite nonzero operands. Integer `/` casts to `Float64` first, so it takes the reciprocal too.

Secondary: the `floordiv` docstring (expr.py#L6702-L6745) says Polars "first does the floating-point division ... and then performs the flooring". With a literal divisor that is `floor(x * (1 / c))`: `pl.col("x") // 49.0` on `x = 49.0` is 0.0 on a frame of two rows or more.
repro: On the streaming engine, a frame shorter than the thread count streams as one-row morsels and gives the IEEE values, so which result a row gets depends on the morsel length (polars-double-scalar-divisor).
handling: Nothing to work around: sverify follows the engine's behaviour, which the facts record. The fix is in Polars's documentation. Suggested fix: list the reciprocal for a scalar divisor among the user guide's exceptions, with the subnormal case, or drop the reciprocal for divisors whose reciprocal overflows.
found_by: the Polars characterization reverse pass (2026-11-04): the docstrings and user guide at py-2.1.0 checked against each open fact
